description: Proof for the graph-nodes-wide / graph-edges-wide contract (data-plane/graph-wide.md). Every styled panel is paired with an unstyled control, and every styled panel achieves its effect with fieldConfig.overrides alone — no plugin-local per-item mechanism. The ECharts relations panel cannot read the wide form yet (todo/graph-wide-migration.md), so the five per-mark demonstrations use core panels, whose marks are already fields.

panels.description:
**Wide edges frame, four per-edge overrides — the whole point of the contract.**

Fixture = worked example 3, with a leading `row` string column as the categorical row dimension. Each of the four edges is a numeric field, so each is addressable by `byName`:

- `a-->c` — a fixed colour (`dark-red`)
- `b-->d` — `custom.hideFrom` (Viz + Legend + Tooltip): the bar is simply gone
- `a-->b` — Unit `ms`, Decimals 0
- `c-->d` — Unit `s`, Decimals 2

Compare with the control on the right. All four are impossible in the legacy row format, where every edge shares the `mainstat` column.
panels.title: Wide edges — four per-edge overrides

panels.description: **Control.** Identical query, `overrides: []`. Four bars, palette colours, no units, nothing hidden.
panels.title: Control — same wide edges, no overrides

panels.description:
**Wide nodes frame, per-node colour and per-node units.**

Fixture = worked example 4, wide form. One numeric field per node, reduced by `reduceOptions.calcs[0]` — the replacement for the `mainstat` column.

- `a` — fixed colour `dark-red`, Unit `ms`, Decimals 0
- `b` — Unit `percentunit`, Decimals 2 (so `8` reads as `800.00%`)
- `c` — untouched

Two nodes with *different* units is the demonstration: core's Node graph has one "main stat unit" panel option for every node at once.
panels.title: Wide nodes — per-node colour and per-node units

panels.description: **Control.** Identical query, `overrides: []`. Three palette-coloured bars, no units.
panels.title: Control — same wide nodes, no overrides

panels.description:
**A data link on exactly one node.**

Same wide nodes fixture. `config.links` is set by a `byName` override on field `a` only, so `a`'s value renders as a link and `b`/`c` do not — visible without clicking.

This is gap 1 of `todo/relations-data-links.md`: in the legacy form a link lives on the `mainstat` *column*, so it paints on **every** node and `${__data.fields.id}` can vary only its destination, never its presence.
panels.title: Wide nodes — a data link on exactly one node

panels.description: **Control.** Identical query, `overrides: []`. No cell is a link.
panels.title: Control — same wide nodes, no links

panels.description:
**The migration path, end to end.**

This is the *unmodified* legacy edges CSV from [sankey.json](./sankey.json), run through **Convert field type** (`mainstat` → number) and then **Rows to fields** with **no options at all**.

Auto-detection takes the first string column (`id`) as the field name and the first numeric column (`mainstat`) as the value; every other column falls through to `field.labels`. The column headers below are the resulting display names — `e1 {source="gateway", target="api"}` — which is `field.name` followed by the label set.

The `convertFieldType` step is mandatory: with no numeric field, `rowsToFields` silently returns its input unchanged.

targets.csvContent:
id,source,target,mainstat
e1,gateway,api,1200
e2,gateway,web,800
e3,api,auth,650
e4,api,db,900
e5,auth,db,300
e6,db,api,120
e7,web,api,450

panels.title: Legacy CSV → wide, via Rows to fields (no options)

panels.description:
**The "before".** The same legacy CSV with no transformations, rendered by the ECharts relations panel as it works today. Seven edges, one `mainstat` column, no per-edge anything.

The override picker on this panel lists exactly `id, source, target, mainstat` — four fields for seven edges — which is the wall `todo/relations-item-overrides.md` documents.

panels.description:
**Dense, edge-per-field.** Worked example 5: three nodes fully connected is six edge fields — the N·(N−1) growth. Every ribbon stays individually addressable, and `b-->a` carries a fixed colour to prove it at density.

At 30 nodes this form is 870 fields, which is the ceiling the contract states.
panels.title: Dense — edge-per-field (6 fields for 3 nodes)

panels.description:
**Dense, adjacency matrix.** The same six edges, produced from the *legacy* dense CSV by core's **Grouping to matrix** (Column `target`, Row `source`, Cell `mainstat`). Four fields instead of six, and the count grows as N rather than N².

Note what the transform actually emits: the key column is named `source\target`, the target columns appear in first-appearance order rather than sorted, and the frame is **not square** — a node that never appears as a source gets no row.

The override on column `a` is the normative rule: **a matrix column is a node**, not its inbound edges. Per-edge config is unavailable here, because an edge is a cell.

targets.csvContent:
id,source,target,mainstat
a-->b,a,b,10
a-->c,a,c,20
b-->a,b,a,30
b-->c,b,c,40
c-->a,c,a,50
c-->b,c,b,60

panels.title: Dense — adjacency matrix (4 fields for 3 nodes)

panels.description:
**Ranged edges — one frame per edge, no aggregation.**

Four TestData series, aliased with edge ids, standing in for a Prometheus `time_series` instant/range query with `legendFormat: {{client}}-->{{server}}`. This is the `graph-edges-multi` variant: the value field is named `Value` in every frame, so `getFieldDisplayName` substitutes the frame name and each series is identified by its edge id.

`a-->c` carries a fixed colour, proving each edge is addressable. The hazard is on the same page: `byName: Value` would match **every** edge at once, because the raw field name is shared.

The legacy form cannot consume this at all — it needs one row per edge, which is why `docs/relations-data-sources.md` requires instant queries plus two SQL Expressions.
panels.title: Ranged / multi — one frame per edge, reduced by calcs[0]

panels.description:
**The gap this contract does not close on its own — expected to error today.**

The same wide edges fixture as the top-left panel, handed to the ECharts relations panel. `frameToNodeGraph` requires fields literally named `source` and `target`, finds none, returns `null`, and `buildOption` throws.

That is not a graceful degradation, and fixing it is phase 1 of [todo/graph-wide-migration.md](../../../todo/graph-wide-migration.md): detect the wide shape, read it, and surface a notice rather than an exception. This panel is kept as the regression target.
